prerequisites: Basic mathematical knowledge from the first year.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the terminology and conceptual, logical, and physical models used to represent production systems.
Know the main production configurations and the characteristics of capacity, flow, flexibility, and integration.
Understand the technical and economic criteria for selecting and sizing components and industrial projects.
Know the principles of production programming, inventory management, maintenance, simulation, and digital twin.
Configure and dimension a production system according to product and market characteristics.
Choose and analyze a layout, dimensioning its fundamental elements.
Perform capacity analyses and simple economic evaluations and comparisons between alternatives.
Apply procedures for grouping products and machines and interpret simulation and flow monitoring models.
Compare configurations, layouts, and industrial projects based on technical and economic criteria.
Evaluate production constraints and resource performance.
Interpret data related to reliability, failures, and maintenance to guide decisions on production resources.
Describe production systems, models, and indicators with appropriate terminology and illustrate the criteria and evaluations used in alternative analysis.
Develop the ability to integrate knowledge of design, programming, and maintenance of production systems and to independently explore digital tools for simulation, monitoring, and decision support.

syllabus_topics: Models and data for production: Representation of products, manufacturing cycles, resources and orders; data necessary for planning and controlling production activities. Classification of production systems according to material and information flows; capacity, throughput, flexibility and integration as characteristics and indicators of the system.

Economic evaluation of machines and industrial projects: Analysis of industrial costs and relationship between costs and production volumes; breakeven point. Determination of the economic value of an industrial machine; present value and main indices for comparative evaluation of industrial projects.

Analysis of production configurations. Layouts by department, in-line and by cell; product and cycle data necessary for flow study; criteria for comparing configurations. Group Technology and application of product and machine grouping procedures.

Production planning: Calculation of effective resource capacity, determination of the number of machines and analysis of production constraints; batch production and comparison between inventory management models. Role of ERP systems in data sharing and coordination of production, warehouse and procurement. Principles of lean production and Just in Time; operation of pull systems and electronic Kanban: consumption acquisition, generation of replenishment signals, information updating and monitoring of flows between production phases.

Work study and simulation of production flows: Organization of the workplace and association/scheduling between operators and machines. Introduction to discrete event simulation to represent resource operation and evaluate capacity, waiting times and utilization levels.

Monitoring and maintenance of resources. Failures, reliability and operational life of machines; maintenance policies, intervention times and availability. Introduction to predictive maintenance with machine state detection techniques, evolution towards machine learning for anomaly recognition and support for maintenance decisions.

Digital twin of production systems: Principles of digital modeling of machines and production processes; connection between the model and data from the physical system. Use of the digital twin to monitor performance and evaluate operational scenarios.
assessment_rules: The final grade is the sum of the points obtained, expressed out of thirty. Each of the three questions is evaluated from 0 to 10 points, considering content correctness, clarity of exposition, and depth of analysis. The exam is passed with an overall score of 18/30 or higher.
